demoted._parameter: C orders the parameter position in the grammar itself: `...` is only ever last, and `void` alone is only ever the whole list, so one alternation repeated by commas necessarily accepts `f(..., int x)`. Both members are concrete node types occurring nowhere else, so facet membership selects exactly the nodes the supertype would have.

uncategorised.reason: the declarator spine of a type with no name in it — the `[]` of `char (*)[8]`
the same, for the `(void)` of `int (*)(void)`
the same, for the parentheses that group it
the same, for the `*`
the declarator spine of a reference type with no name in it — the `&` of `void f(int&)`

`public`, `private`, `protected` as a bare keyword: in a base clause it says how a base is inherited, and with a colon it forms an `access_label`. It is deliberately not a `_modifier` — admitting it as one made `class W { public int x; };`, a `public:` with the colon left out, parse as a field with a modifier
the parenthesised argument list of a call; its elements are `_argument`
the same, for `[n]`

GCC's assembler name on a declarator — `extern int errno __asm__("__errno_location");`. It is not an `_attribute`: an attribute is valid in half a dozen positions, one of which starts a statement, and admitting this there would give `__asm__("nop");` a second reading as an attribute plus an empty statement
`volatile`, `goto` and friends on an asm statement. `_modifier` is defined over declarations and an asm statement is not one
one entry inside an attribute specifier's list; the specifier around it is the `_attribute`
a declarator carrying a GNU attribute; the attribute is the `_attribute` and the declarator is inside it

which named cast this is — `static_cast`, `dynamic_cast`, `const_cast`, `reinterpret_cast`. It is a field of the cast rather than a construct of its own, and collapsing the four into one node is exactly what this exists to avoid

the comma operator. Not a member of `_expression`, and C's own grammar draws the same line — it splits `expression` from `assignment-expression` because a comma inside an argument list separates arguments. Admitting it into `_expression` would make `f(a, b)` ambiguous with `f((a, b))` at every call in the corpus
a stray `;` at file scope, which C23 allows and every compiler accepted long before it. It declares nothing
the braced enumerator list, for the same reason
one backslash escape inside a string or character literal
`__extension__`, which suppresses a pedantic diagnostic. It alters no meaning, so it is not a `_modifier`, and it annotates nothing, so it is not an `_attribute`
the `.field` of a designated initializer
a braced initializer; it is a value rather than a body, and its elements are ordinary `_expression`s
`.field = v` — a designator and a value. It binds a POSITION, not a name, so it is not a `_binding`
the `[…]` that opens a lambda. It is what makes a lambda recognisable at its first character, which is the only reason `[` in expression position is tractable at all
the `=` or `&` that opens a capture list and says what the unlisted names do
the parenthesised parameter list of a declarator; its elements are `_parameter`
the same, for the parentheses that decide whether `*` or `[]` binds first
the concrete declarator spine: what a name is wrapped in to say it is a pointer. The name inside it is the `_name`; the wrapper declares nothing on its own
the raw tail of a directive, taken as one token because its content is not C — a macro body is text until it is expanded
the `defined X` operator, which exists only in a conditional's condition and is not an expression of the language — its operand is a macro name, and an undefined one is legal here and nowhere else
the `#word` of a directive this grammar has no rule for: `#pragma`, `#error`, `#line`
`__has_include(<x.h>)`, for the same reason: its operand is a header name, not an expression
a function-like macro's parameter list, which is not a `_parameter` position of the language — the names it binds are text, not values
the `&` or `&&` after a member function's parameters, which says which value category the object must have
the declarator spine of a reference: what a name is wrapped in to say it is `T&` or `T&&`. Same status as C's pointer declarator, which declares nothing on its own
the `[3]` or `[0 ... 7]` of one
the `<int, 4>` of an instantiation. Its elements are types and expressions rather than `_argument`s: a template argument is an argument to the COMPILER, not to a callable
the `<typename T>` of a template. Its elements are `_parameter`s and are listed there; the list itself is the bracket around them

a type plus an abstract declarator, in the positions where a type is an OPERAND: a cast, `sizeof`, a template argument, an alias declaration. Not a member of `_type`, which is threaded over the type specifiers — and C++'s own grammar agrees, giving `type-id` a nonterminal of its own. In C it is covered through `_argument`; C++ does not admit a bare type where an argument goes, so here it needs an entry

a macro in a namespace head or body — `namespace std _GLIBCXX_VISIBILITY(default) { … }`, `_GLIBCXX_BEGIN_NAMESPACE_VERSION`. It is the hole the preprocessor would have filled: not a declaration, not a statement, not a directive. Reachable from those two positions only, and the ledger says why
